findings.title: queued default is evaluated once at import, not per instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created in the process carries the same process-start timestamp instead of the time the assignment was queued. The value is serialized into the Celery task payload via to_dict(), so the recorded time is wrong for every event. It should use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: from_dict silently fails open, disabling the loop guard with no log
findings.body: from_dict() swallows TypeError and returns None. `cls(**input_dict)` raises TypeError for any unknown key, so a payload written by a newer producer that added a field (or any malformed payload) yields None. The sync_assignee_outbound task then treats the assignment as having no source, should_sync() stops blocking the originating integration, and the Jira -> Sentry -> Jira cycle this PR is meant to stop comes back. Nothing is logged, so the regression is invisible. The safety check fails open silently; at minimum the parse failure should be logged.

findings.title: New task kwarg breaks mixed-version workers during deploy
findings.body: sync_group_assignee_outbound now always sends an `assignment_source_dict` key in apply_async kwargs (None when there is no source). Messages enqueued by the new code during a rolling deploy will be consumed by workers still running the old sync_assignee_outbound signature, which has no such parameter, so they fail with an unexpected-keyword TypeError. That exception is not in the retry exclude list, so the messages retry and are then dropped. The rollout ordering or signature compatibility should be addressed and called out.

findings.title: No test that a different source integration still propagates outbound
findings.body: The new test only covers the case where the assignment source is the same integration as the linked external issue. Nothing verifies the other half of the contract stated in the code comment: a source from a different integration must still propagate outward. A bug that suppresses all outbound sync whenever assignment_source is set would pass the whole suite. A case with a second integration as the source, asserting that the outbound call happens, is needed.

findings.title: to_dict test cannot detect the queued timestamp bug and no round-trip test exists
findings.body: test_to_dict only asserts `queued is not None`, which passes even with the import-time default. There is no test that `AssignmentSource.from_dict(source.to_dict())` round-trips, although that is the exact path the Celery task uses to rebuild the source from the payload. A round-trip test and a check that queued reflects creation time are missing.

findings.title: New assignment_source parameter on sync_status_outbound is never passed or used
findings.body: The abstract sync_status_outbound gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but nothing in this PR passes it and no implementation reads it. Status sync is not gated on the source at all, so the parameter suggests protection that does not exist while changing an abstract contract that implementers must now consider. It should either be wired through and used or removed.

findings.title: Task now passes new positional and keyword args to every installation
findings.body: The task calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` positionally and `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)` unconditionally. Any installation whose should_sync override still takes one argument, or whose sync_assignee_outbound does not accept **kwargs, will raise TypeError on every assignment. The new tests mock ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound with a MagicMock that accepts anything, so they cannot catch this. The concrete integration implementations are not in this diff and should be checked.
